assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling made aryl amines routine; ligand design (bulky electron-rich phosphines) turned an unreliable transformation into a general, predictable method used from discovery chemistry to process scale. Exactly the kind of bond-forming tool that changed how chemists everywhere build molecules.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic systems and ligand families that made the reaction broadly useful; Kosugi's tin-amide precedent was earlier and stoichiometric-in-tin, so a two-person prize is cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Adoption is overwhelming in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with decades of independent confirmation; recognition is arguably overdue, though the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be seen as having covered related ground.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Relative weight of Kosugi's earlier precedent is my recollection and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions with simple catalysts, enabling transformations hard to achieve by two-electron chemistry. Wide uptake in methodology, late-stage functionalization and industry; conceptual simplicity is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan reported the 2008 synthetic breakthroughs that launched the field; Nicewicz, Konig, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre contributed important parallel or later work, so allocation is contestable. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), which may weigh against him.
assessment.maturity: Field is mature enough to judge: thousands of papers, commercial reactors, and applications in pharma. Dual catalysis with nickel is a strong extension.
uncertainties: Prior prize to MacMillan complicates the configuration.
Credit between the 2008 groups and earlier photochemistry (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, Cano-Yelo/Deronzier) is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating C-H bonds as functional groups; directing-group, ligand-enabled and undirected approaches have shortened syntheses and enabled late-stage modification. Strongly aligned with efficiency in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-enabled, remote and enantioselective C-H activation), Sanford (Pd/Pt-mediated oxidative functionalization, directing groups) and Hartwig (borylation, undirected) each made distinct decisive contributions; Daugulis and Smith are also credited, so the field is broad and the configuration is not obviously clean.
assessment.maturity: Broad confirmation and increasing industrial adoption, though selectivity and scope for unbiased substrates remain limited, so some may consider it still developing.
uncertainties: Hartwig overlaps with B002, which may constrain how a committee can combine candidates.
Fragmentation of the field across directing-group, undirected and borylation strategies may make a compact prize difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors use engineered deaminases to convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a conceptually new chemical editing of DNA with therapeutic impact. From my synthetic perspective the question is what is new chemically: here, evolved enzyme chemistry applied to a nucleobase in situ, which is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Liu led; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor) were the first-author inventors. Kondo and Nishida's earlier deaminase-targeting work is credited and might complicate attribution. Liu's prime editing is a separate candidate.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation has begun with early trial results, but long-term outcomes are limited; recognition may be slightly premature, and the 2020 prize already honored genome editing.
uncertainties: Border-field with biology; novelty as chemistry is debatable.
Overlap with the CRISPR prize and with B028 for Liu.
Long-term clinical safety evidence is not established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes created a new class of ligands and organocatalysts; N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous in organometallic catalysis, including metathesis catalysts, and in main-group chemistry. A clear conceptual and practical advance in molecular chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline NHC (1991); Bertrand reported stable (phosphino)carbenes earlier (1988) and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes; Nolan developed NHC-metal catalysts. Bode and Rovis cover organocatalysis, a different branch. A Arduengo-Bertrand pairing is natural, with Nolan optional.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and wide use; timely or overdue, though some value was already rewarded via the 2005 metathesis prize.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's 1988 carbene and Arduengo's 1991 NHC is sometimes debated.
Whether a third laureate is needed for catalysis applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation enabled chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical, and allowing modified proteins to be studied. A genuine methodological advance in synthetic chemistry with wide uses.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported NCL in 1994 (with Muir and others on later expressed protein ligation); Danishefsky, Brik and Liu contributed extensions. Kent-Dawson-Muir seems the most defensible core.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over three decades, with applications in chemical biology; recognition reasonable, though routine protein expression has reduced some demand.
uncertainties: Credit among Kent, Dawson, Muir and Danishefsky could be disputed.
Impact is narrower than the very broad methods above.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave controlled radical polymerization of many monomers with defined architectures, a general synthetic method with industrial relevance in materials. Controlled polymerization is a genuine chemical control of bond formation.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski (Cu-mediated ATRP, 1995) and Sawamoto (Ru-catalyzed living radical polymerization, 1995) were simultaneous; Wang is co-author of the first Matyjaszewski paper. Kamigaito is a collaborator of Sawamoto. RAFT (B009) is a competing candidate with similar claim.
assessment.maturity: Established and widely used; industrial penetration of ATRP specifically is moderate and RAFT competes, which may split recognition.
uncertainties: Choice between ATRP and RAFT recognition is unresolved.
Industrial impact relative to scale of use is only my approximate recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders convert ligand binding into target destruction via induced proximity with E3 ligases, a new therapeutic modality that drug discovery is rapidly adopting. Medicinal chemistry design of heterobifunctional molecules is chemically interesting but I would ask what is new chemically beyond design logic.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs (2001); Ciulli provided structure-guided design and VHL ligands; Handa, Ito and Kim relate to thalidomide/cereblon molecular glues. Splitting between PROTACs and glue-degrader biology is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials ongoing, no approved PROTAC drug yet to my knowledge, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Attribution between PROTAC and molecular-glue discoveries is complicated.
